title: FakeCompanyABC — Traditional RAG
heading: Measure first, then improve the pipeline
text: The experiments were intentionally staged: establish a dense baseline, inspect its failures, reduce policy-space noise, test reranking, and only then evaluate answer generation. 01 HR corpus 5 fictional Markdown policies → 02 Chunking 400/80, 700/120, 1000/150 → 03 Nomic + Chroma Dense semantic retrieval → 04 Failure analysis Exact evidence + source relevance → 05 TF-IDF routing Select likely policy file(s) → 06 Optional reranker Cross-encoder Top-5 → Top-3 → 07 Qwen generation Grounded Top-3 context → 08 Evaluation RAGAS + secondary judge + manual check

title: FakeCompanyABC — Traditional RAG
heading: Fully local baseline
text: Embeddings: nomic-embed-text (768-D) Vector DB: ChromaDB Generator: qwen3:0.6b Local judge: qwen2.5:1.5b-instruct + RAGAS

title: FakeCompanyABC — Traditional RAG
heading: Retrieval before generation
text: Ground truth stores exact source evidence, allowing Hit@K, Recall@K, Precision@K and MRR to be measured without depending on the generator.

title: FakeCompanyABC — Traditional RAG
heading: CPU-conscious
text: Latency was measured because an improvement that is too expensive on CPU is not automatically the preferred system.

title: FakeCompanyABC — Traditional RAG
heading: Dense baseline, then chunking and failure analysis
text: The first 20-question benchmark showed that Top-3 coverage was already strong, but additional chunks often came from the wrong policy.

title: FakeCompanyABC — Traditional RAG
heading: Initial dense retrieval · 20 questions
text: Metric K=1 K=3 K=5 Hit@K 0.800 1.000 1.000 Recall@K 0.775 1.000 1.000 Precision@K 0.800 0.367 0.220 MRR — — 0.883 Interpretation: the required evidence was normally present by Top-3, but extra retrieved chunks diluted precision.

title: FakeCompanyABC — Traditional RAG
heading: Chunking experiment
text: Size / overlap Chunks Hit@1 Recall@1 Recall@3 Prec@3 MRR@5 400 / 80 38 0.800 0.725 0.950 0.383 0.892 700 / 120 22 0.800 0.775 1.000 0.367 0.883 1000 / 150 16 0.700 0.650 1.000 0.367 0.825 700 / 120 was selected: complete Recall@3 with fewer chunks than 400/80; 1000/150 reduced first-rank quality. Failure diagnosis: dense retrieval was usually finding the answer, but semantically similar language from unrelated HR policies could enter Top-3. This shifted the research question from “how do I retrieve more?” to “how do I keep the search space cleaner?”

title: FakeCompanyABC — Traditional RAG
heading: Policy routing fixed the main source-level error
text: TF-IDF was used only to select likely policy files. Dense Nomic retrieval still ranked chunks inside that candidate search space. Query User question No manual keyword rules → Route TF-IDF policy scores Up to 2 candidate files; fallback when weak/ambiguous → Embed Nomic query vector search_query: prefix → Retrieve Chroma Top-3 Dense search within selected scope

title: FakeCompanyABC — Traditional RAG
heading: 20-question source-cleanliness result
text: 15 / 60 wrong-policy chunks · dense → 2 / 60 wrong-policy chunks · routed ≈87% reduction in wrong-policy chunks. Questions containing any wrong-policy chunk dropped from 11/20 to 1/20 .

title: FakeCompanyABC — Traditional RAG
heading: Why a new metric was needed
text: Exact Evidence Precision@3 stayed at 0.367 , because a correct-policy chunk can be useful without containing the exact evidence string. Source Precision@3 exposed the improvement: Dense only ~.750 TF-IDF + dense ~.967

title: FakeCompanyABC — Traditional RAG
heading: Ranking on the original 20 questions
text: 16 / 20 first evidence at rank 1 18 / 20 within rank 2 20 / 20 within rank 3 · MRR@3 0.883 Because all 20 questions already had correct evidence inside Top-3, the benchmark was too easy to meaningfully study reranking. This motivated a harder 100-question set.

title: FakeCompanyABC — Traditional RAG
heading: Harder 100-question retrieval benchmark
text: The benchmark deliberately includes paraphrases, scenarios, thresholds, negative conditions, location rules, approval conditions, historical/current distinctions and cross-policy questions. 64 hard questions 36 medium questions 51 multi-evidence 19 multi-source 100 total questions

title: FakeCompanyABC — Traditional RAG
heading: Final three-system comparison · Top-3
text: Metric Dense only TF-IDF + dense TF-IDF + dense + reranker Hit@1 0.730 0.790 0.840 Hit@3 0.990 1.000 1.000 Recall@3 0.938 0.938 0.947 Evidence Precision@3 0.420 0.413 0.420 Source Precision@3 0.847 0.950 0.963 MRR@3 0.850 0.888 0.917

title: FakeCompanyABC — Traditional RAG
heading: Ranking-quality snapshot
text: Dense · MRR@3 .850 Routed · MRR@3 .888 Reranked · MRR@3 .917 The cross-encoder improved first-relevant ranking for 11 questions, worsened 7, and left 82 unchanged.

title: FakeCompanyABC — Traditional RAG
heading: CPU latency trade-off
text: Stage Average Nomic query embedding 64.32 ms Dense after embedding 1.76 ms TF-IDF + dense after embedding 2.97 ms TF-IDF + dense + reranker after embedding (cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2) 401.08 ms Approximate total retrieval: ~66 ms dense, ~67 ms routed dense, ~465 ms reranked. Selected retrieval design: TF-IDF + dense. The reranker achieved the best aggregate ranking metrics, but policy routing delivered most of the practical benefit for almost no additional CPU latency.

title: FakeCompanyABC — Traditional RAG
heading: Grounded generation and judge comparison
text: The generator was deliberately kept small so that retrieval and grounding quality remained visible rather than being masked by a large model's prior knowledge. Route TF-IDF Policy candidate selection → Retrieve Nomic + Chroma Top-3 context → Generate qwen3:0.6b Context-only HR answer → Judge A RAGAS + Qwen2.5 Local, reproducible → Judge B GPT-5.6 Sol Same saved answers; secondary evaluation

title: FakeCompanyABC — Traditional RAG
heading: Final four-case generation comparison · 100 questions
text: Pipeline Judge Faithfulness Factual correctness Semantic similarity Answer relevancy Dense RAGAS + Qwen2.5 0.801 0.652 0.779 — TF-IDF + Dense RAGAS + Qwen2.5 0.754 0.668 0.778 — Dense GPT-5.6 Sol 0.831 0.753 — 0.912 TF-IDF + Dense GPT-5.6 Sol 0.848 0.775 — 0.921

title: FakeCompanyABC — Traditional RAG
heading: Context changed
text: 36 / 100 questions had different retrieved context after routing

title: FakeCompanyABC — Traditional RAG
heading: Answer changed
text: 32 / 100 generated answers changed

title: FakeCompanyABC — Traditional RAG
heading: Manual judge check
text: 5 representative questions reviewed manually GPT-5.6 Sol aligned much better with the manual judgments than the smaller local judge in this small spot-check. Interpretation: generation scores are diagnostic, not absolute truth. The disagreement between judges became a result in itself: evaluator quality can become an evaluation bottleneck.

title: FakeCompanyABC — Traditional RAG
heading: A simple routing layer beat complexity on the accuracy/speed trade-off.
text: The project showed that retrieval should be diagnosed before adding heavier components. TF-IDF policy routing substantially cleaned the search space at negligible cost; cross-encoder reranking improved ranking further but added ~400 ms CPU latency. The resulting classical pipeline is preserved as the baseline for the GraphRAG study.

title: FakeCompanyABC — GraphRAG
heading: Build the graph in validated stages
text: The graph is treated as an engineered representation, not as an automatic LLM by-product. Each intermediate stage is inspected before the next one is trusted. 08.1 Schema discovery spaCy candidates → embeddings → PCA/HDBSCAN → manual review → 08.2 Entity extraction GLiNER spans + type + confidence + offsets → 08.2.1 Entity validation Interactive full-corpus inspection → Next · 08.3 Relation extraction Build relations only after entity quality is validated → Future Neo4j + GraphRAG Validated graph retrieval compared with the classical RAG baseline

title: FakeCompanyABC — GraphRAG
heading: Let the corpus suggest the ontology, then review it manually
text: Candidate concepts were collected from the policy corpus, embedded with Nomic, projected with PCA, clustered with HDBSCAN, and manually reviewed into a domain-specific schema. Input HR policies Clean Markdown + 700/120 chunks → Candidates spaCy NER + noun phrases → Represent Nomic embeddings 768-dimensional vectors → Explore PCA + HDBSCAN Structure candidate concepts → Review Manual curation Merge, split, reject noisy clusters → Output 25 entity types Reviewed GLiNER schema

heading: PCA view of candidate concepts

title: Artificial Intelligence of Things–Enabled Sleep Monitoring Using Wearable Inertial Sensors and a Transformer–CNN Model
heading: Paper overview
text: Neendh-T is a compact Transformer–CNN model for sleep–wake detection from wrist-worn actigraphy. Evaluated on the MESA Sleep benchmarks, it combines competitive classification performance with low-latency inference on a smartphone, Raspberry Pi, and desktop CPU, supporting sleep monitoring without cloud inference.

title: Generisch-Net: A Generic Deep Model for Analyzing Human Motion with Wearable Sensors in the Internet of Health Things
heading: Paper overview
text: Generisch-Net is a generic BiGRU–CNN model for several wearable-IMU human-motion tasks rather than one problem-specific network. The study evaluates the same model for activity recognition, closed-loop person re-identification from gait, and emotion recognition.

title: From Steps to Sentiments: Cross-Domain Transfer Learning for Activity-Based Emotion Detection in Wearable IoT Systems
heading: Paper overview
text: This study introduces Jazbat-Net, a lightweight model that transfers representations learned from a large wearable human-activity dataset to emotion recognition from gait. It evaluates smartwatch and smartphone inputs and demonstrates compact, on-device emotion inference.

title: HHARNet: Taking Inspiration from Inception and Dense Networks for Human Activity Recognition Using Inertial Sensors
heading: Paper overview
text: HHARNet is a one-dimensional convolutional network for wearable-sensor human activity recognition, inspired by the multi-branch structure of Inception and the feature connectivity of DenseNet. It is evaluated on two public inertial-sensor activity datasets.

title: Smart-Wearable Sensors and CNN-BiGRU Model: A Powerful Combination for Human Activity Recognition
heading: Paper overview
text: This work presents a lightweight CNN–BiGRU model for classifying human activities from smartwatch and smartphone inertial data. It studies compact acceleration-magnitude inputs alongside higher-dimensional sensor configurations on the WISDM 2011 and WISDM 2019 datasets.

title: Spak-Net: A Lightweight Convolutional Neural Network for Activity Recognition with Wearable Inertial Sensors
heading: Paper overview
text: Spak-Net is a lightweight convolutional network for sports and general activity recognition from wearable inertial sensors. Its addition-based architecture has only 398 trainable parameters and is evaluated on the IM-Sporting Behavior and WISDM-11 datasets with edge deployment in mind.

title: UltaNet: An Antithesis Neural Network for Recognizing Human Activity Using Inertial Sensors Signals
heading: Paper overview
text: UltaNet investigates an antithesis architecture for wearable human activity recognition: a gated recurrent unit is followed by convolutional layers with different kernel sizes. The model is evaluated using the public WISDM inertial-sensor dataset for ambient-assistive applications.

title: Machines Perceive Emotions: Identifying Affective States from Human Gait Using On-Body Smart Devices
heading: Paper overview
text: This study recognizes six basic emotions from human gait captured by body-mounted inertial sensors using a CNN–BiGRU model. It also investigates reducing the input to magnitudes of three-dimensional acceleration and angular velocity to lower computation while retaining strong classification performance.

title: Khail-Net: A Shallow Convolutional Neural Network for Recognizing Sports Activities Using Wearable Inertial Sensors
heading: Paper overview
text: Khail-Net is a shallow convolutional network for sports activity recognition from wearable inertial sensors. With 1,251 trainable parameters, it is designed as a resource-conscious model and is evaluated on sports activities as well as a benchmark WISDM human-activity dataset.
